item.title: DSS-EVAL: Verified Recall and Abstention Precision
item.dc:creator: Dual Substrate
item.description: Public benchmark results demonstrating perfect abstention precision and high multi-hop recall on small ledgers, along with honest documentation of current gate limits.
item.content:encoded:
Governed memory is only as trustworthy as the verifiable tests behind it. Rather than making sweeping claims about universal intelligence, DSS publishes exact micro-benchmarks on the open DSS-EVAL suite.

Key metrics from the latest published run:

  • Perfect Abstention Precision (1.000): Across 300 test queries per seed, the retrieval router abstained from answering whenever source truth was absent, avoiding hallucinations.
  • Sub-millisecond Routing: Retrieval-router lookups consistently measure under 1 ms across small ledgers with hundreds of versioned entries.
  • Honest Limitations: The evaluation also highlights what is not yet finished, including our two open integrity gates and current 0.14 recall@1 ranking track on dense ablated benchmarks.

item.title: Lineage and Prime-Indexed Coordinates
item.dc:creator: Dual Substrate
item.description: How prime-indexed coordinates maintain parent-child derivations directly from ledger records, allowing agents to trace provenance without black-box vector drift.
item.content:encoded:
Retrieval systems frequently depend on opaque vector databases where data associations drift over time as embedding models evolve or index weights rebalance.

DSS grounds memory in mathematical structure:

  • Prime Coordinates: Each ledger entry is assigned a coordinate derived from prime indexing, where shared factors denote structural relationships like parentage, derivation, and thematic clusters.
  • Traceable Ancestry: When an agent synthesizes a conclusion, it records the exact coordinates of the entries it drew upon. Anyone can walk the lineage tree backwards from conclusion to source.
  • Rebuilt from Truth: The retrieval index is completely reproducible from the underlying git repository. If an index is corrupted or questioned, it can be regenerated deterministically from the commit history.

item.title: Principals and Grants in Governed Memory
item.dc:creator: Dual Substrate
item.description: Every human operator and every runtime agent acts as a named Principal with passkey identity. Grants define exact access windows to versioned ledgers rather than global API keys.
item.content:encoded:
In traditional application stacks, agents share broad database credentials and global model keys. When an agent produces an unexpected answer or performs an unintended write, identifying the authorizing context requires digging through disjointed server logs.

In the Dual Substrate System, identity and authorization are structural:

  1. Principals: Humans, organizations, and autonomous agents are registered as first-class Principals authenticated via passkeys and decentralized identifiers.
  2. Grants: Permissions to read, append, or bind models to ledgers are issued as discrete, versioned Grants managed in the Control Plane.
  3. Boundaries: An agent cannot interact with surfaces or memory outside its active grant window.

Because grants are immutable records stored directly in the governed state, accountability is verifiable at the storage layer rather than reconstructed after the fact.

item.title: About
item.dc:creator: Dual Substrate
item.description: What the Dual Substrate blog is for and how it relates to the product.
item.content:encoded:
This blog documents the Dual Substrate System: governed memory, lineage, and evaluation for agents that must stay accountable to people and policy.

It is separate from the marketing site but aligned with it. Essays and claims here explain mechanisms; the product lives at dualsubstrate.com.

What you will find

  • Platform: principals, grants, ledgers, and surfaces.
  • Lineage: coordinates, retrieval, grounding, and memory policy.
  • Proof: benchmarks, DSS-EVAL, and known limits.
  • Notes: shipping updates and operator-facing detail.

Benchmarks

Open evaluation artifacts and methodology pointers live with DSS-EVAL on GitHub.
